![](images/2c/2c96a0fc119984b83ba68a0cfc50540563a3ea76cc887d3e184238250773e91b.png)

Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$$
\displaystyle x = t^{2} + 2t + 1, y = \frac{2}{3}t^{3} - 2t
$$
from $t =-3$ to $t = 2$ (shown above)?
corrected_content.worked_solution: Differentiate: $x'=2t+2$, $y'=2t^2-2$. Their squared sum is $$4(t+1)^2+4(t^2-1)^2=4(t^4-t^2+2t+2).$$ Hence $$L=2\int_{-3}^2\sqrt{t^4-t^2+2t+2}\,dt.$$ The square root keeps the speed nonnegative on the entire interval, including where $t+1$ changes sign.
